clue.text: Strapping Roger is what started it all

parts.note: strapping means big and burly
to roger is slang for to have sex with, as is to bang

explanation.surface: A lusty man named Roger is blamed for kicking off some saga.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roger' looks like a name but is the British slang verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmological theory holds that the universe began in one primordial explosion.

clue.text: Omitting Brown's last outburst, do some quick electioneering

parts.note: bar means except, omitting

indicators.note: last means the final letter of the name

parts.note: a storm is an outburst, as of protest

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown, Labour leader, rushes around campaigning without his final tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Omitting' looks like an instruction to delete; it gives a word meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: To barnstorm is to tour quickly giving campaign speeches.

clue.text: Lead on energy chief hoarding top grade

indicators.note: hoarding means keeping the letter inside

parts.note: go means energy, get-up-and-go
head means chief
A is the top mark

explanation.surface: An energy boss grabs the best rating.
explanation.definitionFit: Go ahead is an instruction to proceed, the same as telling someone to lead on.

clue.text: Pass oneself off as a rising, fabulous storyteller

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: to pose as is to pretend to be

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming fabulist pretending to be someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' here means writing fables, not marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop is the ancient Greek author of the fables.

clue.text: Sex act producing generous climax?

parts.note: giving means generous
head means the top or climax, as in come to a head

explanation.surface: A sexual act that ends generously.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving head is slang for oral sex.

clue.text: Hat fit? Not pissed then!

definitions.note: incapable is a jokey word for blind drunk, so its opposite means sober

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat
fit as in able to do something

explanation.surface: Someone whose hat still sits properly is evidently sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed' here is British slang for drunk, not angry; 'drunk and incapable' is a stock British police phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Being still able to function, rather than drunk and incapable, means you have not had too much.

clue.text: Chuck's group of luvvies

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as chuck is, to throw
second meaning: the actors in a play; luvvies are actors

explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck's' looks like a man's possessive but is 'chuck is'. Luvvies is British slang for gushing theatre people.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for throwing and the noun for all the performers in a production.

clue.text: Brief Bell on energy for when there's a large audience

definitions.text: for when there's a large audience

parts.note: to brief someone is to prime them
Tim Bell, Thatcher's advertising and PR guru

explanation.surface: A short PR man's pitch gets airtime when viewers flock in.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Tim Bell was the publicist behind Margaret Thatcher's election campaigns.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime time is the evening slot when television audiences are biggest.

clue.text: Spray Queen? Extremely unwise during fight

indicators.note: during means placed inside

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters of the word

parts.note: the first and last letters of unwise

explanation.surface: Using a spray on a gay man in a scrap would be rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spray' looks like a verb; it is a bunch of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray is a small bunch of cut flowers, which is a bouquet.

clue.text: One leaves forced evacuation to last of Tory opposition

indicators.note: leaves means the letter departs, with another taking its place

parts.note: an enema forces the bowels to empty
a means one

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the word

parts.note: the final letter of Tory

explanation.surface: A Tory MP is forced out, then the opposition takes over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forced evacuation' suggests a war zone; it is a medical procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: The enemy is the opposing side in a conflict.

clue.text: Lots of topless fantasies

indicators.note: topless tells us to remove the top letter of the word

parts.note: dreams are fantasies

explanation.surface: Plenty of daydreams about bare-chested people.
explanation.definitionFit: Reams, literally bundles of paper, is an informal way of saying a large quantity.

clue.text: Lobby for underwear with single blue variation

parts.note: a vest is an undergarment in British usage
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a variation of the word blue gives its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Campaigning for underpants available in a new single shade of blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lobby' poses as a verb meaning campaign; it is the noun for an entrance hall. In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestibule is an entrance hall or porch, the same room as a lobby.

clue.text: A kiss aroused her bedroom activity lover, Blair, on leaving

parts.note: sleeping is what most people do in a bedroom
a beau is a boyfriend

indicators.note: leaving says the word on departs from the name

parts.note: Tony Blair, the British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A smutty tale of a woman excited by a kiss, with Blair's sex life as he leaves office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bedroom activity' promises something racier than it delivers.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale the cursed princess sleeps for a century until woken by a prince's kiss.

clue.text: See 11
It should ensure a stiff one doesn't go to waste

definitions.text: It should ensure a stiff one doesn't go to waste

parts.words: It should ensure a stiff one doesn't go to waste
parts.note: a stiff is slang for a corpse, and going to waste is decaying; the process preserves dead bodies

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a stiff drink, or something ruder; 'stiff' is slang for a dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: Embalming preserves a corpse from decay with chemicals.

clue.text: Reserve is said to calm an excited member

definitions.text: said to calm an excited member
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Speaker of the Commons calls this word to quieten rowdy MPs, members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Holding back is supposedly how to cool down an aroused organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' points rudely elsewhere; it is a Member of Parliament, and the Speaker's cry is 'Order! Order!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for booking ahead and the Speaker's call for calm in the House of Commons.

clue.text: Altering Brenda's flipping prancing

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, the letters read backwards

parts.note: Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen, ER
jigging is dancing about

explanation.surface: The Queen is changing her flipping cavorting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British swear word; it signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rejigging means rearranging or changing something.

clue.text: I'm shafted, screwed — awkward that

indicators.note: screwed means twisted up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being cheated and ruined, calling it embarrassing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screwed' reads as more slang for being cheated, but it signals the scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ham-fisted means clumsy and lacking dexterity, like someone with hams for hands.

clue.text: Greatly discounted the gossip — so tawdry!

parts.note: dirt means scandalous gossip
cheap means tawdry, shoddy

explanation.surface: A huge price cut on a rag full of sleazy tittle-tattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dirt cheap is sold at a very low price.

clue.text: Latin girl squeezing Latin boy's pot

indicators.note: squeezing means holding the other name tightly inside

parts.note: Maria is a typical Latin American girl's name
Juan is a typical Latin American boy's name

explanation.surface: A Latina hugging her boyfriend's cooking vessel, or his stash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin' suggests the classical language; here it means Latin American.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is common slang for cannabis, the drug also called marijuana.

clue.text: Short spell in desolation makes stress an embarrassing fact

indicators.note: in means the short word is put inside the longer one

parts.note: ruin is desolation
a bit is a short while

explanation.surface: A brief period of bleakness rubs your nose in something shameful.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub it in is an idiom for keep reminding someone of an awkward or painful matter.

clue.text: Hooligan goes topless, showing boner

indicators.note: goes topless tells us to drop the first letter

parts.note: a terror is an unruly troublemaker

explanation.surface: A yob strips off his shirt and reveals an erection.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface 'boner' is the crude word, but its older meaning is a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A boner, in older slang, is a silly blunder, the same as a mistake.

clue.text: Brian's making love with trout!

indicators.note: making means forming the letters into something else

parts.note: Brian's read as Brian is, the name's letters
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Brian is having sex with a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The rainbow is a common species of trout.

clue.text: To boot a slapper inside in the West Indies

definitions.note: names a place, so the answer is a West Indian island

indicators.note: inside places this word within the other

parts.note: to boot means too, in addition
bag, as in old bag, is a rude word for a woman, like slapper

explanation.surface: Kicking a loose woman while in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boot' suggests kicking; 'to boot' is the idiom meaning also. A slapper is British slang for a promiscuous woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is the smaller island of the Caribbean nation Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: Dirty Digger's organ represented by 'x'

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a newspaper owned by Rupert Murdoch, Private Eye's Dirty Digger
second meaning: the multiplication sign is read as this word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' sounds anatomical; it is a newspaper. Private Eye calls the Australian Murdoch the Dirty Digger.
explanation.definitionFit: The London newspaper owned by Murdoch shares its name with the word said for a multiplication sign.

clue.text: 'Names' surprisingly need interest on bill, not a retainer

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests these letters turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: i is the symbol for interest in finance
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Lloyd's Names need interest on their bill, not paying a lawyer's retainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retainer' suggests a fee or servant; here it is one who retains memories.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with amnesia has lost memories, so cannot keep hold of what happened.

clue.text: Dick, topless, is a hot piece!

indicators.note: topless means losing the first letter

parts.note: member is a euphemism for penis, as is dick

explanation.surface: A shirtless man described as sexy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot piece' suggests an attractive person; it is a glowing coal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a glowing fragment of coal or wood left in a dying fire.

clue.text: Be half lovey-dovey with Clinton?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... is half of the phrase ... and coo, to whisper lovingly
second meaning: the first name of US President Clinton

explanation.walkthrough: Doves bill and coo; billing alone is half of that courting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for lovebirds touching beaks and the first name of the US President.

clue.text: Topping old lady's diametric alternative

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of the letters of diametric

explanation.surface: An extreme choice of killing off your mum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' is British slang for killing; 'old lady' is slang for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Matricide is the killing of one's own mother.

clue.text: Anger surrounds Blair's opening — likely to get bashed by evangelist?

definitions.text: likely to get bashed by evangelist?

indicators.note: surrounds means the first word goes around the letter

parts.note: bile means bitterness or anger

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the name

parts.note: the first letter of Blair, the Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Rage greets Blair's speech, and a preacher may thump him.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bible-basher is a forceful evangelist, so the book gets bashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealous preacher is called a Bible-basher, from thumping the scriptures.

clue.text: One taken in by Engel's new republic

indicators.note: taken in by means placed inside the rearranged word
new means the letters of the name are formed afresh

explanation.surface: Someone is fooled by Engels's new state.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a West African republic.

clue.text: Be sick though not downcast

definitions.meaning: second meaning: cast up rather than down

explanation.walkthrough: 'Downcast' suggests sadness; here it is cast down, whose opposite is thrown up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for vomiting and also literally hurling something upwards.
